learningObjective: Interpret generated Triton code emitted by TorchInductor and identify what the code does and does not tell you about performance.

canonicalClaims.claim: Generated Triton code exposes the fused iteration space and load/compute/store structure, confirming which ops were fused; runtime performance also depends on autotune configurations, which are visible in @triton.autotune decorators but chosen at first call.
conditions: TorchInductor with the Triton codegen backend.
nonImplications: Does not imply reading source replaces profiling.
Does not imply autotune always converges to the optimum.

misconceptions.whyWrong: Autotune choices and launch configuration change latency substantially.

misconceptions.claim: Inductor codegen is frozen across 2.x versions.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Codegen strategy evolves substantially across minor releases.

misconceptions.claim: Reading Triton source is unnecessary once profiling is done.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Source review answers 'what was compiled'; profiling answers 'how it ran'. Both are useful.
It runs once per configuration space and caches the best.
